text: Every NASA dataset records change. Trend Detective finds what is changing on Earth, where, how much, and whether it is real.
This is the guided tour. Everything you will see is computed live from NASA records.

Take Cairo. The Change Studio tests eight NASA POWER climate variables and a drought index with one method, and ranks them. Night-time temperature is changing most, rising about zero point four degrees per decade.
The seasonal fingerprint shows when in the year it is changing. Dots mark months that survive false discovery rate control.
This climate spiral replays forty-five years of monthly anomalies. As the loops drift outward, from blue to orange, Cairo's nights are getting warmer.
Is it real? We shuffled the years two thousand times. Not one shuffle looked as trended as the real record, and it passes the autocorrelation and multiple-testing checks.
It is not just one model. Twenty-five years of quality-screened NASA MODIS satellite data, from Microsoft's Planetary Computer, independently confirm the night-time warming.
Where is it changing? The trend map repeats the test on every grid cell around Cairo. Every cell is warming, and more than half are significant after field-wide correction.
Some change is visible from space. Swipe between NASA MODIS images of the Aral Sea, in two thousand and in twenty twenty-four.
At ten metre resolution, land-cover maps show Egypt's New Administrative Capital rising from the desert east of Cairo.
Finally, analog intelligence compares today's trends with past episodes on the same tectonic plates, and only shows forecasts whose skill was verified at unseen sites.
Search any place on Earth and start investigating. Trend Detective. Find what is changing, and prove it.
